key_findings.finding: For bladder-preserving trimodality treatment of MIBC, accepted concurrent radiosensitizers include 5-FU plus mitomycin C (the BC2001-tested combination), cisplatin, and gemcitabine; the evidence retrieved directly supports 5-FU/mitomycin and notes cisplatin or mitomycin/5-FU as guideline-preferred options. If choosing from the combinations listed, 5-FU plus mitomycin C is an established, evidence-based concurrent regimen; cisplatin-containing doublets should not be assumed to be radiosensitizing regimens merely because they are systemic chemotherapy combinations.

source_tools.relevance: Guideline search result reports BC2001 randomized evidence: concurrent 5-FU plus mitomycin C with RT improved locoregional DFS and OS compared with RT alone.

key_findings.finding: Do not conflate concurrent radiosensitization with systemic perioperative or metastatic regimens: cisplatin-gemcitabine is a standard systemic regimen in metastatic urothelial cancer and cisplatin-based chemotherapy is used perioperatively, but this does not establish cisplatin-gemcitabine as a standard concurrent RT doublet.
